subject: chemical_engineering

resources.title: Process Dynamics, Operations, and Control
resources.notes: Chemical-engineering course with lecture notes, problem sets and written assignments covering dynamic process models, feedback/feedforward control, stability, tuning, sensors and valves.

resources.title: Integrated Chemical Engineering Topics I: Process Control by Design
resources.notes: Integrates material/energy balance modeling, dynamic simulation, controllability, heat-exchanger networks and off-normal process behavior; includes problem sets and computational tools.

resources.title: Chemical and Biological Reaction Engineering
resources.notes: Covers reaction rates, stoichiometry, equilibrium, kinetics, chemical and biochemical reactors, catalysis, heat/mass transport and material/energy balances.

resources.title: Transport Processes
resources.notes: Assessed undergraduate course in heat and mass transfer, conduction, diffusion, radiation, convection and interphase transport. Includes problem sets, recitations, laboratory work, quizzes and examinations; useful for instructional and verification evidence rather than reference-only coverage.

resources.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
resources.notes: Graduate chemical-engineering thermodynamics covering classical and statistical thermodynamics, transient open/closed systems, stability and equilibria, property models, and multicomponent phase and chemical equilibria. Includes extensive problem work and exams.

resources.title: Advanced Thermodynamics
resources.notes: Modern graduate thermodynamics with lecture videos/slides, homework and exams; covers multicomponent and chemical equilibrium, electrochemical potentials, nonequilibrium thermodynamics, membrane equilibria and transport coupling. Cross-departmental source; mappings remain limited to explicit chemical-engineering taxonomy keys.

resources.title: Fundamentals of Advanced Energy Conversion
resources.notes: Cross-departmental assessed course applying thermodynamics, chemistry and transport to energy conversion/storage, hydrogen, fuel cells, batteries, combustion and catalysis; includes problem sets and projects.

known_gaps: foundation and beginner chemical-engineering instruction remains incomplete
dedicated open separations curriculum with assessments remains thinner than transport and thermodynamics
hands-on process simulation training with a verified open license remains needed
research references and graduate courses do not by themselves establish expert readiness
expert readiness requires runtime retrieval, practical projects, verification/validation and passed assessment
